transcript:
[00:00] Sam Fletcher: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync for Catalyst Health. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: Jordan here.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Maya on the line.
[00:10] Ethan Park: Ethan here.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood.
[00:14] Sam Fletcher: Great. We're 45 minutes, we'll focus on the SDK tool-calling work and structured output issues you reported. Priya, quick status?
[00:32] Priya Nair: Yeah so last week we shipped the SDK patch that changes the function-call payload shape, it should make the signature more explicit - node and python examples updated in the repo. We saw some successful runs but Maya flagged intermittent 500s when the tool returned an empty body.
[00:51] Maya Chen: Correct - on staging we saw a few 500s, stack trace points to our adapter layer but there might be something on the Redwood side, especially around streaming + function callback. The error looks like: "null body parser failed" - the logs are attached in the shared drive link (https://drive.redwood/example-logs).
[01:12] Priya Nair: I pulled the logs, thanks. There're two places to check: one is the SDK serializer that wraps tool responses into the function result object; two is the runtime fallback when streaming stops early - sometimes the KV cache state ends up meaning the call is incomplete.
[01:32] Jordan Lee: Sorry, quick question - when you say KV cache, is that the per-session cache of previous tokens? Our SRE used the term K V cache in the notes, spelled out, we weren't sure.
[01:43] Sam Fletcher: Yeah, sorry we say KV cache, that's the key-value attention cache used to speed subsequent tokens. It shouldn't affect tool payloads, but if streaming terminates mid-chunk it could cause the runtime to mark the call as incomplete.
[02:01] Maya Chen: The failing requests were the ones where our adapter returned a 204 No Content. Maybe our adapter should return an explicit empty JSON object instead of 204. But the SDK used to tolerate that; the patch changed behavior.
[02:18] Priya Nair: Noted. We'll add a tolerance for 204s in the serializer for the next nightly. Also can you share the exact adapter response examples? That will help.
[02:28] Maya Chen: Uploading the sample payloads to the ticket in JIRA shortly.
[02:33] Ethan Park: From a security angle, we need to confirm whether function call payloads are logged in the Redwood managed plane. Our compliance team requires that PII is never logged and that audit logs only show minimal metadata.
[02:46] Sam Fletcher: Good call. Short answer: audit logs include request metadata (model, route, timestamps, token counts) but not full tool payloads by default. We can toggle additional logging but it's opt-in and we can filter fields. We'll send the SOC2 and network diagram to you after the call.
[03:01] Ethan Park: Please do. Also confirm whether KMS is used for keys in the private deployment.
[03:06] Priya Nair: For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. For Dedicated hosted we manage keys but with customer-managed KMS option for enterprise tiers.
[03:16] Jordan Lee: Back to the structured output topic - we want the assistant to return a strict JSON with a known schema (diagnosis_code, confidence, recommended_action). We're using JSON schema validation on our side. But sometimes the assistant emits stray text before the JSON and our parser breaks.
[03:32] Priya Nair: That's a common issue. Two mitigation strategies: 1) use the SDK's structured_output helper which enforces a content-type and will stream only the JSON object, 2) use function/tool calling with a single function that returns the structured payload. We're trying to make both patterns robust.
[03:50] Maya Chen: We tried the structured_output helper - in some cases streaming chunks included notes like "thinking" which end up outside the JSON. Does the helper guarantee the output won't include extra tokens?
[04:03] Priya Nair: The helper wraps output in delimiters and the runtime cleans up prefix/suffix tokens but it's not bulletproof if you call other tools mid-stream. For strict schemas the recommended pattern is function-calling: the assistant calls a function with typed params, the tool returns pure JSON and Redwood returns that as the final structured object.
[04:24] Jordan Lee: Ok that makes sense. We're also concerned about mutation: sometimes the assistant will call the function multiple times during retries and our system creates duplicate records. Any guidance?
[04:36] Sam Fletcher: We recommend idempotency keys on your tool endpoint. When the assistant triggers a function call the SDK includes a request_id you can echo back; use that to dedupe. We're going to add clearer examples in the SDK docs.
[04:52] Maya Chen: Regarding latency: in our internal tests the round-trip for a tool call (assistant->tool adapter->assistant) is ~800-1200ms which is fine, but we saw spikes to 3-4s. Are there known issues with the Dedicated nodes and streaming causing jitter?
[05:09] Priya Nair: Spikes can be due to autoscaling events or cold KV cache priming. For Dedicated we have options: keep-warm instances and prefetching or pinning sessions. Also batching configuration can affect tail latency; smaller batch sizes reduce latency variance but increase cost.
[05:30] Jordan Lee: Can you quantify the cost delta for smaller batch sizes? We need to justify to finance.
[05:35] Sam Fletcher: We'll run a quick cost delta for your workload if you share the token distribution. Priya, can you take that offline?
[05:40] Priya Nair: Yup, will do - please upload a sample token histogram and we'll produce estimates.
[05:45] Maya Chen: We uploaded a small sample corpus earlier to the shared repo (link in ticket).
[05:50] Priya Nair: Got it.
[05:52] Jordan Lee: Also, regarding the SDK integration, are there breaking API changes in the patch? We saw a semver bump but want to confirm upgrade path.
[05:59] Priya Nair: It's a minor semver bump - added stricter validation and a new structured_output helper. Most existing calls should keep working but there are edge cases like the 204 handling we discussed. We'll document upgrade notes.
[06:11] Maya Chen: On the replication of the 500s - we reproduced it locally and it correlates with our adapter returning a 204 for a streaming tool. We'll try returning {} instead to see if that fixes it.
[06:23] Priya Nair: That'd be helpful. Also please include request ID from our logs; it helps us trace on the runtime.
[06:30] Jordan Lee: Quick product question - can Redwood Console show per-route function call counts and failures? That would help us monitor.
[06:38] Sam Fletcher: Yes, Console will show per-route metrics including function-call success/fail counts and per-token latency histograms. It's currently in beta for Dedicated; we'll enable it for the pilot environment.
[06:50] Ethan Park: From security again, we need to ensure egress IPs are fixed during the pilot for allowlisting. Is that supported?
[06:58] Priya Nair: For Dedicated we provide static egress IPs. For Hosted API we can provide a set of IP ranges but not single IPs. For Private you control egress. We'll capture your requirement in the security pack.
[07:12] Jordan Lee: Great. For the benchmark run you mentioned 30k tokens - what's the expected time?
[07:18] Priya Nair: Depends on batch sizes and model choice - roughly 6-12 minutes for a single model pass on Dedicated, maybe longer if we run multiple quantization profiles. We'll coordinate a time window so it doesn't hit production.
[07:30] Sam Fletcher: Let's recap action items then. Priya, reproduce and capture the 500 with KV cache state and SDK logs. Sam, send security docs and pricing. Maya, try changing 204 to {} and push adapter changes to staging. Jordan, upload final token histogram if not already.
[07:48] Maya Chen: I'll push a branch with the adapter change and tag you.
[07:51] Jordan Lee: Uploaded histogram already; will re-check.
[07:54] Ethan Park: Please include a network diagram in the security pack highlighting where the adapter runs.
[08:00] Sam Fletcher: Will do. Anything else?
[08:03] Jordan Lee: One more quick ask - do you have an example of idempotency headers in the SDK? That would be really helpful.
[08:10] Priya Nair: Yes, I'll include example code in the integration gist.
[08:13] Sam Fletcher: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up on the thread and schedule the benchmark next week.
[08:20] Jordan Lee: Thanks, bye.
[08:21] Maya Chen: Thanks.
[08:22] Ethan Park: Bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present (timestamps approximate). Shared artifacts: integration gist (https://github.com/redwood/examples/catalyst-tool-calls), logs link (https://drive.redwood/example-logs), ticket (JIRA-CH-1123).
